mainTopic: Sources for placing altar and מנורה ashes; מעילה on birds not yet fit or past their time, and on קדשים that died
overview: The amud opens by finding sources for where removed ashes are placed. The ashes of the outer altar come from 'ושמו אצל המזבח.' רבי אלעזר learns the ashes of the inner altar from the extra words 'מקום הדשן' in the bird-offering פסוק. He also learns the ashes of the מנורה from the extra letter ה in הדשן. Then a new משנה brings רבי שמעון's view: doves too young to be offered carry מעילה, while pigeons too old to be offered do not. The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's reason. It then explains why the רבנן treat young doves differently from a too-young animal: an animal can be redeemed like a בעל מום, but birds have no פדיון. Next, עולא quotes רבי יוחנן that קדשים that died leave Torah-level מעילה. רב חסדא objects, and after accepting that there is rabbinic מעילה, he asks whether anything can gain מעילה only later. The גמרא suggests blood as an example and begins to answer that blood has מעילה from the start; the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Outer altar has a source, but what about the inner altar?
steps.stepSummary: The rule for the ashes of the מזבח החיצון comes from the פסוק 'ושמו אצל המזבח.' The גמרא asks for the source for the ashes of the מזבח הפנימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the outer altar we know it, because it is written about it: 'And he shall put it beside the altar.' But for the inner altar, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that it has a פסוק for the ashes of the outer altar. Then it asks where we learn the same rule for the ashes of the inner altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the removed ashes must be put beside the altar is written clearly about the מזבח החיצון. Nothing similar is written about the מזבח הפנימי, so the גמרא needs a separate source for it. This question sets up רבי אלעזר's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer altar, in the courtyard, where most קרבנות were burned
The inner (golden) altar inside the היכל, used for incense
From where do we know it? (asking for a source)
Ashes removed from the altar

phrases.english: The outer altar — as it is written about it:
"And he shall put it beside the altar."
The inner altar — from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by setting a known source against a missing one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק teaching that the ashes of the מזבח הפנימי are also put beside the altar.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: an extra verse is applied to the inner altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר cites the bird-offering פסוק that mentions 'the place of the ashes.' Since the outer altar already has a source, this פסוק is applied to the inner altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The פסוק says, 'And he shall remove its crop with its feathers' (and throw it beside the altar, to the place of the ashes). If it is not needed for the outer altar, apply it to the inner altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a source for the inner altar. He uses a second פסוק that also speaks about the place of the ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outer-altar rule is already taught by 'ושמו אצל המזבח,' so a second פסוק about the place of the ashes would add nothing for the outer altar. Using the method of אם אינו ענין, a פסוק not needed for its plain topic is moved to a related topic. Here that topic is the inner altar.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own topic
Apply it to another topic
The crop (food pouch) of a bird
Feathers

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא reads the תורה: a פסוק that seems extra is never wasted, so it is used to teach a new law.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: For the verse says:
"And he shall remove its crop with its feathers" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא א:טז. The part that matters is how the פסוק ends: 'and throw it beside the altar, eastward, to the place of the ashes.'

phrases.english: if it is not needed for the matter of the outer altar,
apply it to the matter of the inner altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְמִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן, תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְמִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ashes of the inner altar are learned from the extra פסוק in ויקרא א:טז, applied by אם אינו ענין.

steps.title: Maybe both verses are about the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe both פסוקים speak about the outer altar, and the second one only tells us the exact spot where the ashes go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: both פסוקים are about the outer altar, and the second one comes to fix its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר. It suggests the second פסוק is not extra after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אם אינו ענין only works if the פסוק is truly unneeded for its own topic. The second פסוק adds a detail, 'eastward,' so it may be needed to tell us exactly where to put the outer altar's ashes. If so, nothing is left over for the inner altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that
To fix its exact place

phrases.english: Say: this and that (both verses)
are about the outer altar,
and the second comes to fix its place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the second פסוק is extra for the outer altar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second פסוק has a job for the outer altar, which is fixing the location, so it cannot be moved over to the inner altar.

steps.title: The extra word 'the ashes' includes the inner altar
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only came to fix the outer altar's place, it could have said just 'beside the altar.' The added word 'הדשן' teaches that even the inner altar's ashes go there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say only 'beside the altar.' Why does it say 'the ashes'? To teach that even the inner altar's ashes are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. It points to an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'beside the altar' would already link this פסוק to the first one and tell us the location. The words 'to the place of the ashes' are therefore extra. That extra wording is what includes the ashes of the מזבח הפנימי.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say (it should have said)
What? Why? (asking what a word comes to teach)
That even

steps.whatToRemember: The ashes of both altars are put in the place of the ashes. The outer altar is learned from 'ושמו אצל המזבח.' The inner altar is learned from the extra words 'מקום הדשן' in the bird-offering פסוק.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"Beside the altar."
What is "the ashes" for?
phrases.notes: He means the words 'to the place of the ashes' at the end of the bird-offering פסוק.

phrases.english: That even the inner altar is included.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לֵימָא קְרָא: ״אֵצֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״. מַאי ״הַדָּשֶׁן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and supports step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to extra wording in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second פסוק is only needed to fix the outer altar's location.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Beside the altar' alone would be enough for the location, so the extra 'הדשן' includes the inner altar's ashes.

steps.title: What is the source for the ashes of the מנורה?
steps.stepSummary: After finding sources for both altars, the גמרא asks where we learn that the ashes of the מנורה also go to that same spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מנורה: where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks one more source question. We have sources for the ashes of both altars, so where is the source for the ashes cleaned out of the מנורה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הדשן was already used for the inner altar in Step 4. So a new hint is needed for the מנורה. The גמרא is setting up the answer that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden Candelabrum in the בית המקדש
From where do we know it? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: The Menorah, from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: He means the ashes and burnt wicks cleaned out of the מנורה. Where must they be placed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the source search from the two altars to the מנורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for placing the ashes of the מנורה in the same spot as the altar ashes.

steps.title: The extra 'the' in 'the ashes' includes the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said 'דשן' (ashes) but said 'הדשן' (the ashes). The extra letter ה adds the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It could have said 'ashes,' and it said 'the ashes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the tiny extra letter ה in the word הדשן teaches that the ashes of the מנורה also go to that spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the whole word הדשן taught about the inner altar. Now the גמרא squeezes one more lesson out of the same word. The extra letter ה ('the') adds the מנורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Ashes
'The ashes'. The added ה is the extra letter the גמרא learns from

steps.whatToRemember: One word gives two lessons. The word הדשן adds the inner altar, and its extra letter ה adds the מנורה. All three kinds of ashes go to the same place.

phrases.english: "Ashes," "the ashes."
phrases.notes: Short for: the פסוק could have written just 'ashes' but wrote 'the ashes,' and that extra ה adds the מנורה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The definite article ה in הדשן includes the ashes of the מנורה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון on young doves and old pigeons
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: רבי שמעון rules that one who uses doves that are too young for an offering is liable for מעילה. Pigeons that are too old may not be used, but there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי שמעון says: Doves whose time has not yet come, one is liable for misusing them. Pigeons whose time has passed, one may not benefit from them, but one is not liable for misusing them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי שמעון argues with the earlier ruling, which said there is no מעילה for both of these birds. He says the young doves do carry מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doves (תורין) are only offered when grown. Pigeons (בני יונה) are only offered when young. The earlier ruling made both cases the same: no benefit, but no מעילה. רבי שמעון splits them. Doves that will grow into fitness carry מעילה, while pigeons that have passed their time do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves. Fit for an offering only when grown
Young pigeons. Fit for an offering only while young
One is liable for מְעִילָה, the misuse of holy property
One may benefit from it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the birds. Doves are 'too young' (their time has not come yet), and pigeons are 'too old' (their time has passed). The two cases go in opposite directions.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרִין שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּן – מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: doves whose time has not arrived, one is liable for misusing them;
phrases.notes: 'Time' means the age when they become fit to be brought as an offering.

phrases.english: pigeons whose time has passed,
one may not benefit from them, and one is not liable for misusing them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה. A new topic after the ashes discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young doves carry מעילה. Pigeons that are past their time are forbidden for benefit but carry no מעילה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reasoning makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רבי שמעון's view, because he states his reason elsewhere. Something that will become fit later is holy even now, since one who brings it outside violates a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Granted, רבי שמעון's view is understood, as his reason is taught: רבי שמעון would say: anything that will be fit after some time, and one consecrated it before its time, he is in violation of a prohibition, but there is no כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says, 'רבי שמעון's view is fine, we know his reason.' It is setting up a question on the other side, the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that something consecrated before its time is still holy enough that bringing it outside is a לא תעשה, though not כרת. Since its holiness takes hold, it makes sense that it carries מעילה. The word בשלמא signals that a contrast with the רבנן is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted. 'This side is fine…' It sets up a question on the other side
He consecrated it
A Torah prohibition
Spiritual cutting off. A harsher punishment

phrases.english: GEMARA: Granted, Rabbi Shimon's view makes sense,
as his reason is taught:
for Rabbi Shimon would say:
anything that is fit after some time,
and one consecrated it within its time,
phrases.notes: 'Within its time' means while it is still too early, before it becomes fit.

phrases.english: he is in violation of a prohibition,
phrases.notes: This is about offering it outside the בית המקדש. The rule is from זבחים 112b.

phrases.english: but there is no karet for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, something consecrated before it becomes fit is already holy, with a לא תעשה but no כרת. That is why it carries מעילה.

steps.title: Why do the רבנן treat young doves differently from a young animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the רבנן: how are young doves different from an animal that is too young (מחוסר זמן), whose holiness still takes hold?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the רבנן: what is different from an animal whose time has not yet come?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the רבנן, who said there is no מעילה for young doves. Why is that different from a young animal that is not yet ready for an offering?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is too young (מחוסר זמן) will become fit later, and it is treated as holy. Young doves are in the same situation, so why do the רבנן say they carry no מעילה? The question points to an inconsistency in the רבנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages. Here, the view in the earlier משנה that young doves carry no מעילה
What is the difference? Used to challenge an inconsistency
An animal that is too young to be offered yet

phrases.english: But the Rabbis:
phrases.notes: He means the ruling of the earlier משנה, that young doves carry no מעילה.

phrases.english: what is different from an animal whose time is lacking?
phrases.notes: An animal too young to be offered yet, which is still treated as holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבָּנַן: מַאי שְׁנָא מִמְּחוּסַּר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא setup of Step 8 by turning to the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling that young doves carry no מעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A young animal (מחוסר זמן) will become fit later and its holiness takes hold. Young doves are the same, so they should also carry מעילה.

steps.title: Too-young animals can be redeemed, birds cannot
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that a מחוסר זמן animal is like a בעל מום, which can get holiness because it can be redeemed. Birds have no פדיון, so an unfit bird gets no holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: an animal that is too young is just like a blemished animal, which can be redeemed. But birds are not disqualified by a blemish, so birds have no redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9: why does holiness take hold of a too-young animal but not of too-young doves?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום can still become holy in the sense that its value can be redeemed (פדיון). A מחוסר זמן animal is treated the same way. Birds are different, because a blemish does not disqualify a bird, so the idea of redeeming a bird does not exist. A bird that cannot be offered yet therefore has no way to become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish that makes it unfit for the מזבח
Redemption: moving the holiness onto money so the animal becomes ordinary
"Just like": the גמרא is comparing one case to another
Birds

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the רבנן are saying a too-young animal is fit to be offered. They are only saying that holiness can take hold of it, the same way it takes hold of a blemished animal that can be redeemed.

phrases.english: They say: an animal whose time has not yet come
is just like a blemished animal,
which is subject to redemption.
phrases.notes: A blemished animal can still be made holy, so that its value can be redeemed.

phrases.english: But these birds,
since a blemish does not disqualify birds,
there is no redemption for birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מְחוּסַּר זְמַן מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַבַּעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 on behalf of the רבנן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (animals can be redeemed, birds cannot)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Too-young doves should be like a too-young animal, so holiness should take hold of them too
steps.terutzMaskana: Holiness takes hold of a מחוסר זמן animal through its ability to be redeemed, like a בעל מום. Birds have no פדיון, so an unfit bird gets no holiness.

steps.title: Sacrificial animals that died leave מעילה
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן: sacrificial animals that died are no longer subject to מעילה by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: sacrificial animals that died are out of the laws of מעילה according to the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: once a sacrificial animal dies, the Torah law of מעילה no longer applies to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead animal can no longer be offered, so it is no longer one of "the holy things of ה׳" that the Torah's law of מעילה covers. The words "by Torah law" leave room for a rabbinic level of מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals that died before being offered
Misuse of holy property, which requires a קרבן and repayment
By Torah law (as opposed to a rabbinic rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the subject of the argument in the next two steps.

phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Sacrificial animals that died
have left the laws of misuse by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected to the theme of when holiness and מעילה apply
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים that died are no longer subject to מעילה by Torah law

steps.title: רב חסדא asks where the holiness went
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects strongly to רבי יוחנן's ruling. These animals were holy, so where did that holiness go when they died?
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא was sitting and teaching this. רב חסדא said to him: Who would listen to you and to your teacher רבי יוחנן? Where did the holiness that was in them go?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges the ruling of step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's logic is that holiness does not just disappear. The animals were truly holy while alive, and death should not erase that, so מעילה should still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or halachic ruling
Holiness
"Where did it go?": a question saying the holiness could not have vanished

phrases.english: Ulla was sitting and saying this teaching,
Rav Chisda said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן שָׁמַע לָךְ וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבָּךְ?!
phrases.english: Who will listen to you and to Rabbi Yochanan your teacher?!
And where did the holiness that was in them go?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמַע לָךְ וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבָּךְ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that dead קדשים leave מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holiness that was really there cannot simply disappear when the animal dies

steps.title: עולא points to the same question on the משנה
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that רב חסדא's question would also hit our משנה. Pigeons that grew too old were once holy, yet the משנה says there is no מעילה on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then let the משנה be difficult too! It says doves whose time has not come and pigeons whose time has passed may not be used, but there is no מעילה. Here too, let us ask: where did the holiness in them go?!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends רבי יוחנן by showing that our own משנה already says holiness can stop bringing מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pigeons that were holy while young and then grew too old once had full holiness. The משנה still rules there is no מעילה on them. So "where did the holiness go?" is not a real objection, because once something can no longer be offered, the Torah law of מעילה can stop.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let it be difficult": then the same problem applies there too
Doves (turtledoves), fit only when grown
Young pigeons, fit only while young
One may not use them, but there is no מעילה if one did
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: Holiness does not automatically mean מעילה. Once an animal or bird can no longer be offered (it died, or grew too old), the Torah law of מעילה may stop, even though using it is still forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: Then let the Mishnah be difficult:
"Doves whose time has not arrived
and pigeons whose time has passed –
one may not benefit from them, but there is no misuse,"
here too let us say:
Where did the holiness that was in them go?!
phrases.notes: He mainly means the pigeons that grew too old. They were once fit and holy, yet the משנה says there is no מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא answers רב חסדא's קשיא from step 12 by turning the same question back onto the earlier משנה, the ruling of the רבנן that step 9 discussed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question: the same objection would apply to an accepted משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Holiness cannot disappear, so dead קדשים must still bring מעילה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה shows that once-holy pigeons that are no longer fit bring no מעילה, so the loss of fitness can end Torah-level מעילה

steps.title: רב חסדא agrees, then raises a new difficulty
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא accepts that there is rabbinic מעילה. He then asks whether anything can have no מעילה at first but gain it later.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I agree with you that there is מעילה by rabbinic law. But this bothers me: is there anything that has no מעילה at the start and then has מעילה in the end?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא agrees with עולא that there is מעילה מדרבנן, so his first question is settled. Then he raises a brand-new problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old question, where did the holiness go, is answered: by Torah law it is gone, but the רבנן still added מעילה. The new problem is about direction. Can something start with no מעילה and only later become subject to it? That pattern seems strange to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit
By rabbinic law, not Torah law
I agree / I concede
At first, from the start
In the end, later

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not rejecting עולא's answer. He fully accepts it and moves on to a separate question.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא answering עולא.

phrases.english: I agree with you
that there is misuse of holy property by rabbinic law.
But it is difficult for me:
Is there anything
that at first has no misuse liability,
and in the end does have misuse liability?
phrases.notes: He is thinking of the doves from our משנה that were too young to be brought.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדֵינָא לָךְ דְּאִיכָּא מְעִילָה מִדְּרַבָּנַן וְקַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts עולא's answer from step 13, then opens a new difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that something with no מעילה at first could gain מעילה later
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holiness status normally starts strong and may weaken. A thing gaining מעילה only later seems to have no example.

steps.title: Blood seems to be exactly that kind of case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. Blood has no מעילה at first but does once it reaches נחל קדרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no such case? But there is blood. At first it has no מעילה, and in the end it does, as the משנה taught: blood at the start has no מעילה, but once it goes out to נחל קדרון, there is מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא by bringing a case that seems to fit his strange pattern: blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא assumed nothing goes from no-מעילה to מעילה. The משנה about blood seems to show exactly that pattern. Blood has no מעילה before the sprinkling, but it does once it flows out to נחל קדרון.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood of a קרבן
At the start, before the sprinkling
The Kidron Valley, outside the Temple
One is liable for מעילה

phrases.english: And is there not?
But there is blood,
which at first has no misuse liability,
and in the end does have misuse liability,
as we learned in a mishna:
Blood, at the start, one is not liable for misusing it;
once it went out to the Kidron Valley, one is liable for misusing it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's assumption from step 14 with a counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that nothing goes from no-מעילה to מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה about blood shows that exact pattern, so such a case does exist.

steps.title: Blood actually has misuse liability from the start
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: blood is not a real example, because it also has מעילה from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: there too, there is מעילה from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the blood question. It is setting up an explanation that continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer denies that blood starts with no מעילה at all. If blood has some kind of מעילה from the start, it does not fit רב חסדא's pattern. The exact explanation of how this works continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that case
Also, too

phrases.english: They say:
There too,
there is misuse liability from the start,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם נָמֵי אִיכָּא מְעִילָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the blood challenge from step 15 by denying that blood starts without מעילה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the counterexample does not really fit the pattern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood has no מעילה at first and gains it later, so it fits רב חסדא's strange pattern.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood also has מעילה from the start, so it is not a true example. The details continue on the next amud.
